options.B: It eliminates the necessity of monitoring vital signs during admission
options.C: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing pharmaceutical products
options.D: It speeds up the physical discharge process for stable patients

explanation: A supportive approach prevents patients from hiding dangerous self-medication habits out of fear of criticism. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h5)

question: How should a nurse respond if a client consistently displays frustration and fatigue during structured group exercises?

options.A: Scold the client for failing to follow group instructions
options.B: Force participation to build physical endurance
options.C: Discontinue all physical activities permanently
options.D: Modify the care plan to adjust activity pacing and intensity

explanation: Recognizing signs of fatigue and frustration allows the nurse and team to adapt the care plan, ensuring activities remain therapeutic rather than stressful. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h5)

question: Why must otic drops generally be administered at room temperature rather than straight from a cold refrigerator?

options.A: Refrigerated drops increase the risk of fungal growth
options.B: Cold solutions instantly crystallize inside the ear canal
options.C: Cold drops trigger severe vestibular vertigo
options.D: Low temperatures destroy the active pharmaceutical ingredients

explanation: Cold fluid entering the external auditory canal stimulates the inner ear's vestibular apparatus, causing acute dizziness and nausea. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T12#GNS215_U6_T12_h3)

question: Why do child development experts advise against prolonged screen time for toddlers in day care centers?

options.A: It causes immediate and irreversible damage to visual acuity
options.B: It prevents children from ever learning how to read books
options.C: It increases the daily caloric intake beyond normal limits
options.D: It hinders active interactive play and essential cognitive stimulation

explanation: Early childhood development relies heavily on tactile exploration, social interaction, and physical movement rather than passive media consumption. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h6)

question: What does the letter 'Q' stand for in the PQRSTU pain assessment mnemonic?

options.A: Quench
options.B: Quality
options.C: Quickness
options.D: Quantity

explanation: In the PQRSTU framework, 'Q' stands for quality, prompting the nurse to ask how the pain feels (e.g., sharp, burning, dull). [learn more](GNS221_U3_T7#GNS221_U3_T7_h4)

question: Why is a home environment assessment essential prior to discharging a patient with mobility impairments?

options.A: To calculate utility bills for financial subsidy applications
options.B: To allow the healthcare team to repossess hospital mobility equipment
options.C: To identify physical barriers like stairs and narrow doorways that impede safe movement
options.D: To test the structural integrity of the community health clinic

explanation: Identifying environmental obstacles beforehand allows families to make necessary home modifications, preventing falls and promoting safety. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h5)

question: Which nursing intervention is a core component of the ventilator-associated pneumonia prevention bundle?

options.A: Keeping the patient completely flat to maximize venous return
options.B: Changing the ventilator circuit tubing every twelve hours
options.C: Administering prophylactic systemic antibiotics to all patients
options.D: Elevating the head of the bed between 30 and 45 degrees

explanation: Head-of-bed elevation significantly reduces the aspiration of gastric contents into the lower respiratory tract, lowering pneumonia rates. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T18#GNS213_U2_T18_h6)

question: What is the primary dietary prescription during the initial acute phase of severe pancreatitis?

options.A: High-protein liquid diet
options.B: Regular solid food diet
options.C: Nil per os (NPO)
options.D: High-fat ketogenic diet

explanation: Keeping the patient NPO reduces pancreatic stimulation by halting the secretion of digestive enzymes during acute inflammation. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h5)

question: Why might a stable patient with sickle cell anaemia have a baseline oxygen saturation slightly lower than normal without immediate distress?

options.A: Pulse oximeters cannot accurately read red cells containing abnormal iron
options.B: Continuous low-grade haemolysis consumes circulating ambient oxygen
options.C: Chronic lung scarring prevents full expansion of the lower alveolar sacs
options.D: The structural nature of HbS shifts the oxygen dissociation curve to the right

explanation: HbS has a lower affinity for oxygen, shifting the dissociation curve to the right, which can result in slightly lower baseline pulse oximetry readings. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T7#GNS311_U2_T7_h4)

question: Why is a computed tomography scan typically preferred over a magnetic resonance imaging scan in the initial emergency evaluation of severe head trauma?

options.A: It provides superior resolution of fine spinal cord white matter tracts
options.B: It eliminates the need for any intravenous access lines
options.C: It is faster and more accessible for detecting acute hemorrhage
options.D: It uses non-ionizing radiation that poses zero physiological risk

explanation: CT scans are fast, widely available in emergency settings, and excel at showing fresh blood and bone fractures. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T13#GNS222_U3_T13_h4)
